q: The flow of electrons from a place of lower potential to a place of higher potential is called an ____.
e: Electron flow is from low potential to high potential. That flow of charge is an electric current. The flow of electrons from a place of lower potential to a place of higher potential is called an electric current.

q: In general, an electric current is a flow of ____ from one place to another.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. In general, an electric current is a flow of electric charge from one place to another.

q: The amount of charge passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in one second is called an ____.
e: Electric current is charge passing a cross-section per second, I = Q/t. The amount of charge passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in one second is called an electric current.

q: The ____ of electric charge through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is called an electric current.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is called an electric current.

q: Current is a ____ quantity by the above definition.
e: By I = Q/t, current is a scalar. Current is a scalar quantity by the above definition.

q: Suppose that the amount of charge $Q$ passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in time $t$, the current $I$ flowing through the conductor is ____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Suppose that the amount of charge Q passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in time t, the current I flowing through the conductor is I = (Q)/(t).

q: If the number of electrons passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is $n$, the amount of charge $Q$ is ____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If the number of electrons passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is n, the amount of charge Q is Q = ne.

q: In the SI system, the unit of electric current is ____ (A) in honour of the French physicist, Andre Ampere.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. In the SI system, the unit of electric current is ampere (A) in honour of the French physicist, Andre Ampere.

q: If the amount of charge ____ passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in 1 second, the current is 1 ampere.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If the amount of charge 1 coulomb passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in 1 second, the current is 1 ampere.

q: Therefore, 1 A is equivalent to ____.
e: 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹, 1 mA = 10⁻³ A, and 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A. Therefore, 1 A is equivalent to 1 C s^-1. 1 c s^-1 is what this sentence is naming.

q: 1 milliampere (mA) = ____ A.
e: 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹, 1 mA = 10⁻³ A, and 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A. 1 milliampere (mA) = 10^-3 A. 10^-3 is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: 1 microampere ($\mu$A) = ____ A.
e: 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹, 1 mA = 10⁻³ A, and 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A. 1 microampere (μA) = 10^-6 A. 10^-6 is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The direction of current is conventionally defined as the direction of the flow of ____ from a higher potential to a lower potential.
e: Conventional current follows positive charge from high potential to low. Electron flow is the opposite arrow. The direction of current is conventionally defined as the direction of the flow of positive charge from a higher potential to a lower potential.

q: Hence, the direction of current is ____ to that of the flow of electrons.
e: Conventional current follows positive charge from high potential to low. Electron flow is the opposite arrow. Hence, the direction of current is opposite to that of the flow of electrons.

q: When an electric current is passed through substances, it can produce three main effects. They are (1) ____ (2) chemical effect and (3) magnetic effect.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. When an electric current is passed through substances, it can produce three main effects. They are (1) heating effect (2) chemical effect and (3) magnetic effect.

q: As an electric current flows through, the ____ wire in the bulb becomes hot and emits light.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. As an electric current flows through, the tungsten wire in the bulb becomes hot and emits light.

q: Practical application of the heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as electric stove, electric iron and ____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. Practical application of the heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as electric stove, electric iron and immersion heater.

q: When a current is passed through copper sulphate solution with copper plates A (anode) and C (____) dipping into it, some copper is deposited on the plate C after sometime.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. When a current is passed through copper sulphate solution with copper plates A (anode) and C (cathode) dipping into it, some copper is deposited on the plate C after sometime.

q: The chemical effect of current is used in charging batteries, purifying metals and ____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The chemical effect of current is used in charging batteries, purifying metals and electro-plating.

q: When a current flows through a coil of insulated wire which is wound round a bar of ____, the bar becomes a magnet and attracts steel pins.
e: When a current flows through a coil of insulated wire which is wound round a bar of soft iron, the bar becomes a magnet and attracts steel pins. Soft iron is what this statement is using.

q: The magnetic effect of current is used in making ____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of current is used in making electromagnets.

q: Electromagnets are used in electrical devices such as electric bell, ____ and electric motor.
e: An electromagnet drives bells, relays, and motors. Electromagnets are used in electrical devices such as electric bell, magnetic relay and electric motor.

q: In 1827 the German physicist ____ found experimentally that at a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends.
e: In 1827 the German physicist Ohm found experimentally that at a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends. Ohm is what this statement is using.

q: At a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is ____ to the potential difference across its ends.
e: At a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends. Directly proportional is what this statement is using.

q: By Ohm's law, the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance can be written as $V = $ ____.
e: Ohm's law: V = IR for a metal at steady temperature. By Ohm's law, the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance can be written as V = IR.

q: Here $R$ is a constant which is called the ____ of the conductor.
e: R is the resistance of the conductor. Ohm's law writes it as V/I. Here R is a constant which is called the resistance of the conductor.

q: The SI unit of the resistance $R$ is ____ ($\Omega$).
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The SI unit of the resistance R is ohm (Ω).

q: Ammeter is a device to measure the current flowing through resistor and ____ is a device to measure the potential difference across a resistor.
e: Ammeter is a device to measure the current flowing through resistor and voltmeter is a device to measure the potential difference across a resistor. Voltmeter is what this statement is using.

q: The potential difference across the resistor is varied by using ____ (variable resistor).
e: The potential difference across the resistor is varied by using rheostat (variable resistor). Rheostat is what this statement is using.

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is the ____ of the potential difference between two ends of a conductor to the current flowing through it.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is the ratio of the potential difference between two ends of a conductor to the current flowing through it.

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is given by the formula ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is given by the formula R = (V)/(I).

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor does not depend on the ____ between its ends and the current flowing through it.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor does not depend on the potential difference between its ends and the current flowing through it.

q: At a given temperature the resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length and ____ to its cross-sectional area.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature the resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length and inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area.

q: The resistance of a conductor is proportional to its length and cross-sectional area as ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of a conductor is proportional to its length and cross-sectional area as R ∝ (l)/(A).

q: $R = \rho \frac{l}{A}$ where $\rho$ is a constant called the ____ of the conductor.
e: R is the resistance of the conductor. Ohm's law writes it as V/I. R = ρ (l)/(A) where ρ is a constant called the resistivity of the conductor.

q: Resistivity of conductor is defined as the resistance of a conductor having one unit cross-sectional area and ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. Resistivity of conductor is defined as the resistance of a conductor having one unit cross-sectional area and one unit length.

q: The unit of resistivity is ____ ($\Omega$m).
e: Resistivity ρ is the material constant in R = ρl/A. Its SI unit is ohm metre. The unit of resistivity is ohm metre (Ωm).

q: If the length or the cross-sectional area of a substance changes, its resistance will also change. But its ____ remains the same.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. If the length or the cross-sectional area of a substance changes, its resistance will also change. But its resistivity remains the same.

q: The resistance of a metal increases with increasing temperature but the resistance of carbon (a non-metal), semiconductor ____ with increasing temperature.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of a metal increases with increasing temperature but the resistance of carbon (a non-metal), semiconductor decreases with increasing temperature.

q: $R_t = R_0(1 + \alpha t)$ where $\alpha$ is a constant called the ____.
e: R_t = R_0(1 + α t) where α is a constant called the temperature coefficient of resistance. The name used here is temperature coefficient of resistance.

q: The unit of $\alpha$ is ____ ($^{\circ}$C$^{-1}$).
e: The unit of α is per °C (°C⁻¹). The unit written here is per °C.

q: A resistor is an electrical device which is used to ____ the electric current flowing in a circuit.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. A resistor is an electrical device which is used to control the electric current flowing in a circuit.

q: It is made of a substance having ____.
e: It is made of a substance having resistance. Resistance is what this statement is using.

q: There are two types of resistors: fixed resistors and ____.
e: There are two types of resistors: fixed resistors and variable resistors. Variable resistors is what this statement is using.

q: A ____ (variable resistor) and its symbol are shown in circuit diagrams to indicate adjustable resistance.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. A rheostat (variable resistor) and its symbol are shown in circuit diagrams to indicate adjustable resistance.

q: The resistors are said to be connected in series if they are connected in such a way that the ____ flows through each resistor.
e: The resistors are said to be connected in series if they are connected in such a way that the same current flows through each resistor. Same current is what this statement is using.

q: If the individual potential differences across the resistors are $V_1$, $V_2$ and $V_3$ respectively, and the total potential difference across the combination is $V$, then ____.
e: If the individual potential differences across the resistors are V_1, V_2 and V_3 respectively, and the total potential difference across the combination is V, then V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3. Leave the relation as V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3.

q: The equivalent resistance of the resistors in series is equal to the ____ of the resistances of the individual resistors.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The equivalent resistance of the resistors in series is equal to the sum of the resistances of the individual resistors.

q: If $n$ resistors of resistances $R_1, R_2, R_3, \dots, R_n$ are connected in series and the equivalent resistance is $R$, then ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. If n resistors of resistances R_1, R_2, R_3, dots, R_n are connected in series and the equivalent resistance is R, then R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3 + dots + R_n.

q: Resistors are said to be connected in parallel if they are connected in such a way that the ____ appears across each and every resistor.
e: Resistors are said to be connected in parallel if they are connected in such a way that the same potential appears across each and every resistor. Same potential is what this statement is using.

q: The current $I$ ____ into three components of current at the point A and flow through the resistors.
e: The current I divides into three components of current at the point A and flow through the resistors. Divides is what this statement is using.

q: For resistors in parallel, the total current is given by the equation ____.
e: Series resistances add. Parallel conductances add, so 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2. For resistors in parallel, the total current is given by the equation I = I_1 + I_2 + I_3.

q: The ____ of the equivalent resistance of resistors connected in parallel is equal to the sum of the reciprocal of the individual resistances.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The reciprocal of the equivalent resistance of resistors connected in parallel is equal to the sum of the reciprocal of the individual resistances.

q: If $n$ resistors of resistances $R_1, R_2, R_3, \dots, R_n$ are connected in parallel and the equivalent resistance is $R$, then ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. If n resistors of resistances R_1, R_2, R_3, dots, R_n are connected in parallel and the equivalent resistance is R, then (1)/(R) = (1)/(R_1) + (1)/(R_2) + (1)/(R_3) + dots + (1)/(R_n).

q: The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by ____ in 1820.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by Oersted in 1820.

q: When a straight wire carrying a current was placed above a compass needle, the needle was ____.
e: When a straight wire carrying a current was placed above a compass needle, the needle was deflected. Deflected is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of the magnetic field due to the current flowing through the wire can be found by using the ____.
e: The direction of the magnetic field due to the current flowing through the wire can be found by using the right-hand rule. Right-hand rule is what this statement is using.

q: Imagine the wire to be grasped in the right hand with the ____ pointing along the wire in the direction of the current.
e: Imagine the wire to be grasped in the right hand with the thumb pointing along the wire in the direction of the current. Thumb is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of the ____ will give the direction of the magnetic field.
e: The direction of the fingers will give the direction of the magnetic field. Fingers is what this statement is using.

q: The magnetic lines of force around the wire carrying a current are ____ around the wire and they are in the plane perpendicular to the wire.
e: The magnetic lines of force around the wire carrying a current are closed circular loops around the wire and they are in the plane perpendicular to the wire. Closed circular loops is what this statement is using.

q: A solenoid is a ____ of wire, which has a magnetic field inside and in its vicinity when a current flows through it.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire, which has a magnetic field inside and in its vicinity when a current flows through it.

q: The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a ____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a bar magnet.

q: When viewing one end of the solenoid, that end will be a south pole if the current is seen flowing in a ____ direction and north pole if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When viewing one end of the solenoid, that end will be a south pole if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction and north pole if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction.

q: If you hold the thumb, the first finger and the second finger of your left hand ____ to each other, with the first finger in the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of the electric current, then the thumb will point in the direction of the motion along which the force acts.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. If you hold the thumb, the first finger and the second finger of your left hand mutually perpendicular to each other, with the first finger in the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of the electric current, then the thumb will point in the direction of the motion along which the force acts.

q: When a ____ moves across a magnetic field it experiences a force.
e: When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field it experiences a force. Charged particle is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of force on that particle is ____ to those of $B$ and $v$.
e: The direction of force on that particle is perpendicular to those of B and v. Perpendicular is what this statement is using.

q: The best method of making a magnet is to use the ____ of an electric current.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. The best method of making a magnet is to use the magnetic effect of an electric current.

q: When a large current flows through the solenoid the steel bar becomes magnetized ____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When a large current flows through the solenoid the steel bar becomes magnetized permanently.

q: Such a magnet is called a ____.
e: Such a magnet is called a permanent magnet. The name used here is permanent magnet.

q: A ____ surrounded by a coil of wire, which acts as a magnet when a current flows through the coil is called a temporary magnet (or) an electromagnet.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A soft iron core surrounded by a coil of wire, which acts as a magnet when a current flows through the coil is called a temporary magnet (or) an electromagnet.

q: It is ____ when the current stops.
e: It is demagnetized when the current stops. Demagnetized is what this statement is using.

q: Increasing the current will create a ____ magnetic field strength.
e: Increasing the current will create a stronger magnetic field strength. Stronger is what this statement is using.

q: Reversing the direction of current will ____ the direction of magnetic field.
e: Reversing the direction of current will reverse the direction of magnetic field. Reverse is what this statement is using.

q: An ____ is an example of the use of the magnetic effect of current.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. An electric bell is an example of the use of the magnetic effect of current.

q: A ____ is also another example of the use of the magnetic effect of current.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. A circuit breaker is also another example of the use of the magnetic effect of current.

q: The electromagnet will attract the iron armature if the current is large, thus ____ the circuit.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. The electromagnet will attract the iron armature if the current is large, thus breaking the circuit.

q: Ammeter and voltmeter are devices for measuring current and ____ (voltage), respectively.
e: Ammeter and voltmeter are devices for measuring current and potential difference (voltage), respectively. Potential difference is what this statement is using.

q: They are constructed based on the principle of a ____.
e: Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. They are constructed based on the principle of a moving coil galvanometer.

q: A moving coil galvanometer is an instrument which is used to ____.
e: A moving coil galvanometer is an instrument which is used to measure electric currents. Measure electric currents is what this statement is using.

q: It is a sensitive electromagnetic device which can measure low currents even of the order of a few ____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. It is a sensitive electromagnetic device which can measure low currents even of the order of a few microamperes.

q: The coil is suspended in a ____ and is free to rotate about a fixed axis.
e: The coil is suspended in a uniform radial magnetic field and is free to rotate about a fixed axis. Uniform radial magnetic field is what this statement is using.

q: A cylindrical ____ is symmetrically positioned inside the coil to improve the strength of the magnetic field and to make the field radial.
e: A cylindrical soft iron core is symmetrically positioned inside the coil to improve the strength of the magnetic field and to make the field radial. Soft iron core is what this statement is using.

q: The spring is used to produce a ____ which balances the magnetic torque producing a steady angular deflection.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The spring is used to produce a counter torque which balances the magnetic torque producing a steady angular deflection.

q: The angle through which the coil is deflected due to the effect of the magnetic torque is ____ to the magnitude of current in the coil.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The angle through which the coil is deflected due to the effect of the magnetic torque is proportional to the magnitude of current in the coil.

q: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting it in ____ with a wire of low resistance called shunt resistance.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting it in parallel with a wire of low resistance called shunt resistance.

q: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting it in ____ with high resistance resistor (multiplier resistor).
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting it in series with high resistance resistor (multiplier resistor).

q: The voltages across the galvanometer and shunt resistance are equal due to the ____ of their connection.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The voltages across the galvanometer and shunt resistance are equal due to the parallel nature of their connection.

q: The relationship between the galvanometer current, shunt current, and their resistances is given by ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The relationship between the galvanometer current, shunt current, and their resistances is given by iR = (I - i)r.

q: The total voltage drop across the voltmeter is given by the equation ____.
e: The total voltage drop across the voltmeter is given by the equation V = i(R + R_v). Leave the relation as V = i(R + R_v).

q: Ammeter is a ____ device.
e: Ammeter is a low resistance device. Low resistance is what this statement is using.

q: Voltmeter is a ____ device.
e: Voltmeter is a high resistance device. High resistance is what this statement is using.

q: Ammeter is connected in ____ with circuit component.
e: Ammeter is connected in series with circuit component. Series is what this statement is using.

q: Voltmeter is connected in ____ with circuit component.
e: Voltmeter is connected in parallel with circuit component. Parallel is what this statement is using.
